To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

i) the National Treatment standard has evolved into a common legal principle shared by international trade and investment law, ii) this common standard has been applied in the new generation EU FTA's, iii) the EU has taken a leading role in promoting the convergence of international trade and international economic law, and iv) the EU has the potential to further develop a unified approach to international economic law in its future FTAs
the EU's new generation FTAs provide a unique opportunity to harmonize the WTO and international investment law approaches to the National Treatment obligation.

i) the "like product" comparator in the WTO and "like circumstances" comparator in international investment law should be harmonized; ii) the "treatment no less favorable than" standard in the WTO and the "fair and equitable treatment" standard in international investment law are substantively similar, but differ with respect to the burden of proof; and iii) the regulatory purpose exception in the WTO and in international investment law is substantively similar but differs with respect to its scope.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions. What are the principal differences between WTO and investment law approaches to the National Treatment principle? What are the principal similarities? How can these differences be reconciled to achieve consistent interpretation across the two legal spheres? What is the role of the EU FTAs in this process?

the following question: what is the appropriate standard of review for the National Treatment provision in new generation EU FTAS, and why is this standard of review consistent with the approach taken by the WTO?
the following questions: 1. What is the relevance of the National Treatment principle for the interpretation of international investment treaties?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in order to achieve a more consistent and predictable application of the National Treatment standard to both international investment and international trade, it is necessary for the EU to harmonize the interpretation of the National Treatment principle across its FTAs, as well as between its trade and investment agreements.
the EU's new generation FTAs represent an important opportunity for the development of a unified and consistent approach to National Treatment across trade and investment law.
the National Treatment standard should be interpreted in the same manner across both international trade and investment law.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EU FTAs have the opportunity to harmonize existing inconsistencies between international investment and trade law, and to create a unified approach to National Treatment.
the EU has a unique opportunity to provide a unified approach to international trade and investment norms, which will benefit the global community.
we are in favor of the EU FTAs to be interpreted consistently across trade and investment protections, and we have provided the basis of why we think that is the case in the body of this Note.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the new generation EU trade agreements provide a unique platform for future investment tribunals to adopt a more coherent approach to National Treatment.

a unified approach to National Treatment across international trade and international investor protections will provide a more coherent and predictable framework for the protection of foreign investment and trade.
, in the context of EU FTAs, a consistent interpretation of the National Treatment standard is not only possible, but also desirable.
